claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is the environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service specifying the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset, the Terraform-compatible API in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, so a separate DNS record/domain is not required.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
The page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ exists and is the state backend guide.
The state backend guide uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, `terraform login`/`tofu login`, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
The TF_TOKEN_* environment variable name for Terraform/OpenTofu credentials incorporates the domain (PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value) and `terraform login`/`tofu login` accept that domain.
